props.title: Gentlemen Broncos

sections.content: Gentlemen Broncos (2009) stands as Jared Hess's bizarre follow-up to Napoleon Dynamite (2004), diving deeper into oddball territory with its story of aspiring sci-fi writer Benjamin Purvis. Like Wes Anderson meets Ed Wood, the film layers multiple narrative levels - we see both the "real" world and visualizations of Benjamin's story "Yeast Lords," performed twice with different actors and styles. Michael Angarano captures teenage creative awkwardness, while Jemaine Clement steals scenes as pompous sci-fi author Ronald Chevalier who plagiarizes Benjamin's work.

sections.content: The film sits in a unique space between celebration and satire of DIY creativity and sci-fi/fantasy fandom. Like Be Kind Rewind (2008) and Son of Rambow (2007), it finds charm in low-budget amateur filmmaking while acknowledging its limitations. The "Yeast Lords" sequences, featuring Sam Rockwell in dual roles, deliberately embrace cheesy effects and overwrought performances that recall straight-to-video 1980s sci-fi like Metalstorm: The Destruction of Jared-Syn (1983).

Director Jared Hess maintains his signature deadpan style established in Napoleon Dynamite (2004), but pushes further into surreal territory. The film's nested narratives and shifting reality recall The Science of Sleep (2006) and Adaptation (2002), though with a distinctly oddball rural Mormon sensibility. Jennifer Coolidge delivers another memorable character performance as Benjamin's nightgown-designing mother, adding to the film's collection of earnest outsider artists. sections.content: While critically dismissed on release, Gentlemen Broncos offers fascinating commentary on artistic ownership and creative authenticity. Like Big Eyes (2014) and American Movie (1999), it explores the complex relationship between "legitimate" and outsider art. The film's treatment of Chevalier's plagiarism echoes real debates about creative inspiration versus theft, while Benjamin's journey reflects broader struggles of finding one's artistic voice amid commercial pressures.
